text:
alex: Quick RFC follow-up — thinking about an "ambient hosting" handshake that lets a client probe capabilities without full secret rebind. wanted to surface tradeoffs.

maria: yes please. tl;dr of what you mean by ambient?

alex: ambient = minimal probe + capability manifest exchange on connect, no long-lived secret push. client asks 'what can you do for me' and runtime replies with features + best-effort routing hints.

jamal: sounds similar to probe-first we discussed, but how do you ensure auth/tenancy guarantees?

alex: auth is delegated: control plane vends short-lived tokens for probes, runtime responds with capability manifest and suggested auth flow. real requests require full credentials.

elaine: worried about sidecarless private deployments — customers want absolute control over creds. can we keep the probe bounded to metadata only?

alex: yes — probe returns non-sensitive capability flags only. example manifest snippet we discussed:

```
{"capabilities":["kv_cache","streaming","quant_profiles"],"probe_endpoint":"/healthz","auth":"probe-token"}
```

sri: ok but what about config drift? if hosted advertises prefix caching but private runtime is misconfigured, apps could degrade. need versioned manifest + checksum.

maria: +1 on versioning. also need an observability contract: when manifest changes, emit event to console and ops.

jamal: fallback behavior? app could prefer hosted for latency but fall back to private -- how do we avoid state divergence (e.g., KV cache prefixes)?

alex: plan: declare stateful capabilities in manifest with compatibility level (strict/compat/none). routing policy will only fallback if compatibility != strict. also document eviction semantics.

ops-bot: deploy:staging succeeded for ambient-handshake-v1 at 2026-03-22T14:12Z :white_check_mark:

elaine: what about telemetry PII? we must ensure manifest doesn't leak region/infra identifiers for regulated tenants.

alex: manifest fields split into public and private sets. public is safe to return to app; private pushed only after full auth inside control-plane channel. we'll add a manifest schema with "scope":"public|private" per field.

sri: how to implement gradual rollout? feature-flag based handshake versioning. clients accept min_version and will degrade to safe path if mismatch. we should add a compatibility matrix to SDK.

maria: ops runbook: on manifest mismatch, notify dev-team, then automatic routing to vetted fallback for 5 minutes while we alert. after that require manual ack.

jamal: one more: network churn and retries. probe-first adds extra RTT. can we cache last-known manifest in SDK and optimistic-route while revalidating async?

alex: yes — SDK will cache manifest with ttl and optimistic mode. must include proof-of-freshness header once revalidation completes.

elaine: doc request: can someone sketch the manifest schema + fallback states? i'll add security review.

maria: i'll sketch it. alex, can you put post-deploy notes in the RFC channel?

alex: will do. thanks all. :pray:
